pa:2611.11531.desc: Jointly selecting layers and modules in transformer foundation models yields better probing features than depth-only or final-layer approaches, and simple fixed strategies recover much of the gain.

pa:2607.13920.name: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
pa:2607.13920.desc: A dynamic stress-testing framework shows that search agents often answer confidently despite unreliable retrieved evidence and may rely on memorized knowledge when documents are factually wrong.

pa:2611.14046.name: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training
pa:2611.14046.desc: A hybrid adversarial training approach combining cross-entropy and KL divergence with geometry-aware perturbations on the confidence manifold improves robustness and transferability by targeting confidence structure deformation.

pa:2611.12872.name: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
pa:2611.12872.desc: A novel multimodal memory framework enhances long-term interaction by combining relational graph expansion of semantic seeds with query-adaptive composition of heterogeneous evidence forms.

pa:2611.17331.name: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
pa:2611.17331.desc: By baking global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, Test-Time Baking (TTB) enhances the fidelity of novel-view decoding in Large View Synthesis Models while maintaining the efficiency of Test-Time Training.

pa:2611.08219.desc: A real-source data synthesis framework trains a 4B agent on 4k task instances with supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, improving realistic productivity work and file-grounded reasoning over larger models.

pa:2611.17060.desc: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. pa:2611.00428.desc: A spectrum can be given to a model as a table in nanometers or as a plot in photon energy, and the decision should not depend on which one it sees. pa:2611.17167.name: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
pa:2611.17167.desc: A decision model that acts poorly can still teach reinforcement learning policies effectively by judging complete action trajectories, improving success on ALFWorld and WebShop.

pa:2611.00359.name: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers

pa:2611.15777.name: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
pa:2611.15777.desc: SO-Arena evaluates System One models across domains and capability families, revealing that scaling and reasoning gains vary and that high overall accuracy does not ensure reliable decision-making.

pa:2611.15094.name: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
pa:2611.15094.desc: A vision-language model trained on nearly one million clinical neuroimaging studies interprets complete examinations, discusses findings in natural language, and outperforms existing general and medical models in diagnosis, localization, reporting, and progression assessment.

pa:2611.17194.desc: Endpoint Distribution Matching Distillation trains a shared fake model only on final student outputs and adds precise teacher supervision to better align few-step diffusion students with teacher distributions for 4-step generation.

pa:2611.14505.desc: Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-AGI tasks, compares memory- and weight-based continual learning under frozen-weight agent harnesses, revealing that harness persistence rarely improves memorization and most harness methods underperform simple caching, while weight-based learning shows better generalization.

pa:2611.17955.desc: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. pa:2611.18550.desc: Distilled few-step diffusion models exhibit diversity collapse because activation variance is concentrated into fewer directions in an intermediate block at the initial denoising step, and ReDiverse restores sample diversity by reintroducing teacher variance directions through adapter fine-tuning or training-free activation steering while preserving generation quality.

pa:2611.14487.name: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
pa:2611.14487.desc: A Twenty Questions-style benchmark for research ideation shows that large language models make most progress early, can recognize good ideas or questions but often cannot generate them, and may benefit from externally sourced candidates in automated research systems.

pa:2611.16312.desc: Robots handle much more than rigid objects: towels, cables, water, sand. pa:2611.19649.name: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
pa:2611.19649.desc: LoopFill reduces decoding latency for looped language models by combining multi-token suffix drafts and shallow-loop predictions into a single draft tree with full-depth verification that preserves the autoregressive output distribution.

pa:2611.20986.name: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
pa:2611.20986.desc: A large language model can output single-chain protein structures from its internal residue states by invoking a pretrained structure head, with reduced long-chain accuracy and MMLU-Pro accuracy in the reported tests.

pa:2611.13685.name: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
pa:2611.13685.desc: A mixture-of-transformers architecture jointly predicts future visual states and actions, leveraging pretrained vision-language representations and egocentric videos to improve robot policy learning without action supervision.

pa:2611.20404.name: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier
pa:2611.20404.desc: Latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, improves compute and data efficiency over standard Transformers, especially when unique data is abundant relative to model size.

pa:2611.16661.name: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
pa:2611.16661.desc: Efficient batch execution of agent tasks is critical to LLM training and development workflows, including benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. pa:2611.21072.zh: 能看懂科學數據與分子結構的超大型AI模型

pa:2611.17110.desc: SALA aligns latent actions across human and robot videos by using language-based semantic similarities to form a shared latent action space that supervises embodied foundation model training and improves robot task performance.

pa:2611.17933.name: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
pa:2611.17933.desc: OutfitterBench evaluates LLM agents managing a 200-day outdoor-equipment rental business under fixed capital and uncertain demand, revealing limitations in sustaining feasible commitments and reallocating resources.

pa:2611.19537.name: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
pa:2611.19537.desc: A framework uses coding agents and a feedback cascade to synthesize code-based policies that achieve long-horizon success and can be factored into a reusable goal compiler for zero-shot transfer to new tasks.

pa:2611.21218.name: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
pa:2611.21218.desc: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that audits and reproduces benchmarks across healthcare roles and capabilities, revealing that model rankings and inference costs vary by context and motivating broader, context-specific evaluation.

pa:2611.20218.zh: 測試AI軟體工程師在真實公司環境的協作能力

pa:2611.19937.desc: An end-to-end flow-matching framework generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories via a cross-asset flow Transformer and a two-stage imitation and group-relative reinforcement learning procedure, improving risk-adjusted returns on cryptocurrency perpetual futures.

pa:2611.14960.desc: Coding agents often find correct patches early but continue working, sometimes undoing correct solutions, with termination lag varying by model and benchmark.

pa:2611.21479.desc: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. pa:2611.04395.desc: Fine-tuning data can include metadata that predicts the correct answer, such as a reward-model score or a quality label. pa:2611.08977.desc: Energy-Based Reasoners guide looped latent reasoning by learning an energy function whose gradient refines states and signals when to stop, with exploration-based training improving performance and efficiency.

pa:2611.21412.name: Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort
pa:2611.21412.desc: MS-HVED enables flexible super-resolution of partially overlapping brain MRI stacks by fusing independently encoded multi-scale Gaussian posteriors with a field-of-view-aware Product-of-Gaussians and physics-informed domain randomisation, improving reconstruction, tissue segmentation, and external clinical generalisation.

pa:2611.17610.desc: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. pa:2611.18330.name: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
pa:2611.18330.desc: Marimba uses frozen Qwen3-ASR features and lightweight readouts to make lexical, turn-end, language, speaker-change, and personal-information decisions from speech, achieving strong detection and calibration on conversational and read-speech benchmarks.

pa:2611.20595.name: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
pa:2611.20595.desc: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. pa:2611.16694.desc: A controlled two-pass audit varying only the revision context reveals that language models often fail to selectively correct errors under disagreement, with expert labels increasing reversals but not reliably improving accuracy, so revision should be assessed using paired conditional metrics per model and protocol.

pa:2611.22115.zh: 國產晶片與開源架構結合的全新智慧助理模型

pa:2611.23143.desc: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. pa:2611.22275.name: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
pa:2611.22275.desc: A decentralized framework enables teams of humanoids to coordinate whole-body loco-manipulation over long horizons using low-level multi-agent post-training and a high-level vision-language planner with speech-based leader-follower synchronization.

pa:2611.23144.name: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
pa:2611.23144.desc: This unified foundation model enables the recovery of dense geometry, camera poses, and object tracking from diverse, uncalibrated observations in 4D scenes using a shared geometry and motion branch architecture.

pa:2611.19244.name: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns

pa:2611.22565.desc: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-represe

We build a higher-order attention layer whose state lives on pairs of items: for a pair (a, b), each third item k is a witness judged through its legs (a, k) and (k, b). pa:2611.20995.name: CONGA: Compiling Gaussian Fiber Geometry for Structured Bayesian Inference
pa:2611.20995.desc: In structured Bayesian models, a large latent block is often Gaussian conditional on a smaller set of parameters, yet generic inference methods relearn this geometry during warmup. We study how this structure can be used to construct transports for posterior inference. The conditional mean and precision determine exact affine maps, including symmetric Brenier and triangular Knothe-Rosenblatt maps,

pa:2611.20003.desc: In 2025 alone, 48 new large language model (LLM) architectures were added to the Hugging Face transformers library, and many of them arrive with a technical report that presents the model as new. What is actually new in these models, and is it tested? We put this question to LLM technical reports. We look at three things: what the reference code shows about how new open-weight architectures differ

pa:2611.18553.name: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
pa:2611.18553.desc: The WEIGHTBENCH benchmark evaluates the capacity of large language models to perform Weight-Space Programming tasks, which involve reading, modifying, and generating the weights of various neural network architectures.

pa:2611.20321.name: Unreasonable Confidence from Simulator Misspecification: Directional Robustness on the SPEED+ Sim-to-Real Benchmark
pa:2611.20321.desc: A simple monocular pose estimator trained on synthetic spacecraft images shows poor real-world transfer, with overconfident pose errors and uneven gains from backbone adaptation and photometric augmentation under different lighting.

pa:2611.24669.desc: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. pa:2611.24941.name: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
pa:2611.24941.desc: UltraTex employs a cascaded multi-view framework that integrates physical knowledge and vision-language model features to accurately generate physically plausible PBR texture maps.

pa:2611.24362.name: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
pa:2611.24362.desc: A novel framework addresses the limitations of current reinforcement learning-based red-teaming methods by employing dictionary learning and on-policy adversarial training to improve the robustness of LLM agents against indirect prompt injection attacks.

pa:2611.24869.name: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
pa:2611.24869.desc: A rule-graph-based generative world model preserves user-defined rules and world states across saving and loading while accurately realizing rule-induced visual changes on designated objects and attributes.

pa:2611.22790.name: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding
pa:2611.22790.desc: Fine-grained questions about long videos ask how many times an action occurs, in what order events unfold, or exactly when a state changes. Answering them can require finding brief moments scattered across hours of footage. Agentic models that decide when and where to look promise to find these moments, yet this ability is hard both to measure and to learn. Sparse supporting evidence may establish

pa:2611.23808.name: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
pa:2611.23808.desc: A diagnostic benchmark and two-phase reinforcement learning framework enable personalized vision-language assistants to jointly connect visual hazard evidence with personal memory for appropriate responses.

pa:2611.24576.name: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
pa:2611.24576.desc: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. Conventional early-exit decoding halts after initial passes without cache completion, truncating cached key-value states of past tokens to shallow depth. We study the opposite strategy, late entry, where new to

pa:2611.24098.name: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
pa:2611.24098.desc: A new benchmark and agentic workflows assess vision-language models for automatic video rough-cut, revealing current models struggle to match expert cut plans.

pa:2607.21179.name: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
pa:2607.21179.desc: ReMo, a training-free method, reduces inference input token cost for omni-modal large language models by compressing redundant visual tokens through cross-modal alignment and replacing object-level visual tokens with compact text descriptions, achieving comparable accuracy on audio-visual tasks.

pa:2611.24681.name: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
pa:2611.24681.desc: A new metric for automatic CAD generation evaluates models through engineering-drawing projections with a saturating penalty along curves, exposing small local errors that volume- or surface-based metrics miss and enabling use as a reinforcement learning reward or test-time verifier.

pa:2611.23824.name: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
pa:2611.23824.desc: Reinforcement learning from terminal answer rewards enables search-augmented language models to interleave reasoning and retrieval without step-level annotations, yet outcome supervision assigns identical credit to every search in a trajectory regardless of whether it retrieved useful information. This limitation is especially severe when all sampled rollouts for a question fail, collapsing group-

pa:2611.24830.name: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
pa:2611.24830.desc: A foundation model fine-tuned from a large language model measures and predicts human behaviour and aligns simulated population responses with human statistics, improving accuracy over frontier LLMs.

pa:2611.24733.name: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration
pa:2611.24733.desc: NPU design-space exploration for LLM inference mainly relies on an expensive simulator that often returns only scalar feedback such as latency and power. Such feedback can rank evaluated configurations, but gives little information for deciding why a configuration is slow or which architecture parameter should be changed next. This limitation is especially severe because prefill and decode workloa

pa:2611.14848.name: Tideway: Phase-Aware Tiered Memory Management for MoE Inference on Consumer Devices
pa:2611.14848.desc: TIDEWAY enables efficient inference of large Mixture-of-Experts models on memory-constrained consumer devices by treating host RAM and GPU VRAM as a unified memory pool with phase-aware layouts and optimized CUDA Graph execution under expert paging.

pa:2611.24738.name: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
pa:2611.24738.desc: Jeveration repurposes a frozen vision-language model to generate coherent images and perform image-to-image and dense prediction tasks in a single forward pass with fast 512x512 generation.
pa:2611.24738.zh: 用現成視覺語言模型快速生成與編輯圖片
pa:2611.24738.why: 不用重新訓練大模型，就能用極快速度產出高解析度圖片並完成影像編輯

pa:2611.21114.name: VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection
pa:2611.21114.desc: Visible artifacts are an unreliable cue for detecting generated videos, because newer generators learn to remove them. We instead detect a trace left by the generation pipeline itself. Most video generators decode latents with a 3D causal VAE that groups consecutive frames in time, so the fidelity of generated frames rises and falls periodically with their position in a group. pa:2611.24154.name: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
pa:2611.24154.desc: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. However, collecting human gameplay is costly, and learning from gameplay videos requires inferring missing actions. Existing datasets also cover a limited range of games, often without explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. To address these gaps, we introduce Game2Player, a framework that

pa:2611.19200.name: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search
pa:2611.19200.desc: Thinking with images empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to use an external Zoom-in tool for fine-grained visual search. Recent works employ supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) with tool-specific designs to enable such capabilities. However, achieving logical reasoning alongside accurate and efficient tool use remains a significant challenge. To address this, we shift t

pa:2611.22033.name: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
pa:2611.22033.desc: Across three shopping benchmarks, increasing large language model shopping agents' thinking effort did not statistically improve product-choice quality but significantly raised reported confidence, and most models were poorly calibrated with correlated errors.

pa:2611.22925.name: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
pa:2611.22925.desc: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few caus

pa:2611.22668.name: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
pa:2611.22668.desc: A multi-view debiasing method aggregates within-class partitions across diverse representation spaces to reduce reliance on spurious correlations and improve worst-group accuracy without bias supervision.

pa:2611.11318.name: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
pa:2611.11318.desc: High-resolution weather prediction is important for resolving local atmospheric patterns missed by coarse global forecasts. Large pretrained weather backbones have improved global forecasting, but adapting them to produce future high-resolution fields from recent coarse states remains challenging and costly. We formulate this setting as Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), a task

pa:2611.23068.name: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
pa:2611.23068.desc: Agent evolution is often bottlenecked by noisy evaluations that cannot reliably identify better candidate artifacts or rank methods, so progress requires making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

pa:2611.21366.name: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
pa:2611.21366.desc: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction. pa:2611.17767.name: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
pa:2611.17767.desc: AnisoFlow learns an anisotropic, learnable prediction target for flow-based generative models, improving FID and image quality without altering the architecture or sampler.

pa:2611.22287.name: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
pa:2611.22287.desc: A method that removes the decoder from latent diffusion models by adding a final-step prediction head to a finetuned diffusion transformer, reducing inference cost and improving pixel quality in image and video generation.

pa:2611.24075.name: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
pa:2611.24075.desc: PACT adapts a pretrained time-series foundation model to new operating conditions by partitioning its frozen embedding space into local charts and learning gated residual transports that preserve previously learned conditions, achieving high macro-F1 with limited labeled calibration data and no condition identity at test time.

pa:2611.24102.name: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents
pa:2611.24102.desc: A step-level inference-time audit detects visual-trigger backdoors in open-weight GUI agents by comparing instruction- and region-induced shifts in decision state against clean-step conformal baselines, localizing triggers with controlled false positives.

pa:2611.23388.name: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
pa:2611.23388.desc: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. pa:2611.21644.name: MInfoVisQA: A Multilingual Benchmark for Information-Rich Visual Question Answering
pa:2611.21644.desc: MInfoVisQA, a 24-language parallel benchmark, reveals substantial cross-language robustness gaps in multimodal large language models for information-rich visual question answering.

pa:2611.23257.name: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
pa:2611.23257.desc: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). pa:2611.23994.name: WaveView: The Novel View Is in the Noise
pa:2611.23994.desc: Generative novel view synthesis (NVS) employs a diffusion model to render a static or dynamic scene from a target camera view. pa:2611.24408.name: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
pa:2611.24408.desc: StrideWorld is a benchmark that fixes references before motion to detect scene deformation and action inconsistency in interactive video world models, showing that most models deform scenes and only depth-scaled command models preserve composed routes.

pa:2611.24161.name: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
pa:2611.24161.desc: Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning combines generative visual reflection with textual reasoning and learns to route between them per input, improving multimodal task accuracy while reducing inference latency.

pa:2611.17600.name: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
pa:2611.17600.desc: LightTAR adapts dimensionality reduction to the prediction task by adding target-aware features from encoder layers via regularized partial least squares, improving multimodal tabular model performance with minimal runtime overhead.

pa:2611.23499.name: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
pa:2611.23499.desc: BiCAT shares a motion representation across arms and conditions each arm's tokens on its partner via symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder, enabling parallel arm token prediction and improving bimanual manipulation success.

pa:2611.23236.name: PGPO: Prototype-Guided Progressive Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
pa:2611.23236.desc: A prototype-guided progressive obfuscation method preserves relative item relations while perturbing high-influence semantic embeddings to defend against inversion attacks in LLM-enhanced recommender systems.

pa:2611.23751.name: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
pa:2611.23751.desc: AnyS1 converts procedural skills into shared decision points, trains a small calibrated pointer model to resolve routine choices, and falls back to a large model when uncertain, reducing cost and latency while preserving reliability.
pa:2611.23751.org: University of Science and Technology of China

pa:2611.24654.name: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
pa:2611.24654.desc: CurvDelta and CurvLoRA constrain LLM updates to a low-curvature preservation space, improving retention while maintaining target adaptation across reasoning, code, and unlearning tasks.

pa:2611.23386.name: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
pa:2611.23386.desc: Chorus shares one set of n-gram embedding tables across all layers, letting each layer project and rescale the embedding using its hidden state, achieving better quality with much smaller tables and lower optimizer memory.

pa:2611.24789.name: HINT-WAM: Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models
pa:2611.24789.desc: World action models (WAMs) have shown promising generalization and data efficiency in robot manipulation by coupling action generation with predictions of future visual dynamics. pa:2611.24651.name: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
pa:2611.24651.desc: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). pa:2611.22673.name: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation
pa:2611.22673.desc: FVSCORE is a neuro-symbolic evaluation framework that compiles videos into prompt and implicit constraint propositions, verifies them with perceptual tools and soft temporal logic, and calibrates significant violations to produce interpretable, human-aligned feedback for video generation.

pa:2611.23779.name: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
pa:2611.23779.desc: A large-scale benchmark of 94 curated biomedical tabular datasets standardizes evaluation across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks and finds that foundation models lead overall while tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain competitive under cost constraints.

pa:2611.22382.name: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
pa:2611.22382.desc: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. pa:2611.21553.name: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
pa:2611.21553.desc: BLIP-Live unifies data, metrics, inference, and training for proactive streaming video understanding, using the PAUC-F metric and achieving state-of-the-art results on proactive streaming benchmarks.

pa:2611.16933.name: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
pa:2611.16933.desc: Kezek separates a mono two-speaker conversation into per-speaker tracks while preserving timing and short replies, using a phase-insensitive speaker-fingerprint-guided two-voice activity model followed by a conditioned time-domain separator, and it improves short-reply retention, leakage, channel-swap, and runtime metrics over an open baseline.

pa:2611.24059.name: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
pa:2611.24059.desc: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). pa:2611.24917.desc: A unified framework, World Snapshot Models, is proposed to train and perform nearly all visual tasks by reformulating them as generation tasks, validated across over 1,000 visual tasks.

pa:2611.17605.name: Choosing Quantized Code LLMs by File Size and Energy per Solved Task
pa:2611.17605.desc: A developer running a code assistant on a laptop downloads one model file, and local inference moves the energy of every request onto that machine. pa:2611.26444.name: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
pa:2611.26444.desc: A diagnostic benchmark of 180 simulated manipulation configurations evaluates whether embodied systems can combine history-based reasoning, precise execution, and closed-loop environmental feedback, revealing that single-view competence does not transfer to composed tasks.
pa:2611.26444.zh: 測試機器手臂如何同時思考與動手做

pa:2611.00911.name: S1CogBench: What System One Decision Models Can and Cannot Do on Cognitive Experiments
pa:2611.00911.desc: S1CogBench evaluates System One decision models on 24 cognitive tasks, revealing that fast decisions often lack evidence-based reasoning and vary widely in reliability.

pa:2611.25980.name: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
pa:2611.25980.desc: AFFECT, an auxiliary objective that trains world models to match visual responses to temporally correlated action noise, improves rollout fidelity and planning success in simulated and real robotic tasks.

pa:2611.20455.name: Embeddings vs. Grep: Rethinking the Dense Advantage in Code Search
pa:2611.20455.desc: Code-search benchmarks show dense encoders well ahead of BM25, yet coding agents do well with grep. What does this dense advantage measure? Existing benchmarks cannot tell: they use curated queries, old code and a handicapped BM25. To find out, we build Repo-Premium, a realistic repository-level code-search benchmark. It ranks files in real repositories, with curated and raw queries in Python, Jav

pa:2611.26414.name: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
pa:2611.26414.desc: ZeroVLN is a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that avoids navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of the VLM brain by using a semantic tool-calling interface and closed-loop reinforcement learning to coordinate a language-based brain with an action expert, improving VLN-CE performance while preserving general visual capabilities.

pa:2611.26298.name: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
pa:2611.26298.desc: A new benchmark, DailySafe, evaluates the ability of multimodal large language models to maintain safety and address evolving risks within complex, multi-turn, real-world interactions.

pa:2611.26629.name: Posterior Matching Distillation
pa:2611.26629.desc: Posterior Matching Distillation trains a stochastic student to match a teacher diffusion model’s full posterior via tilted mean constraints, enabling high-quality few-step image generation without auxiliary score networks.

pa:2611.26510.name: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
pa:2611.26510.desc: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, t

pa:2611.25776.name: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning
pa:2611.25776.desc: VETO suppresses shortcut learning in VideoLLMs by projecting supervised fine-tuning updates onto the orthogonal complement of the text-only activation subspace, improving out-of-distribution video reasoning.

pa:2611.26624.name: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
pa:2611.26624.desc: PlayCraft uses a vision-based player agent and a crafter agent to iteratively revise games, improving player learning gains and slopes across intelligence settings.

pa:2611.24193.name: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
pa:2611.24193.desc: WM^MLLM uses multimodal large language models to maintain an external panorama state with revision history, enabling persistent, editable world generation from a single image with exact revisits and local edits.

pa:2611.26603.name: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
pa:2611.26603.desc: A single scalable network estimates dense metric depth for images and video at native resolution, jointly improving metric accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency.

pa:2611.25387.name: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
pa:2611.25387.desc: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? CAPTCHAs offer a natural test, since humans solve them through this very loop, clicking and dragging on the screen and adjusting after each result. Yet existing CAPTCHA benchmark

pa:2611.26409.name: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
pa:2611.26409.desc: WeMM-Video is a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models that unify text, image, audio, and video processing for joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, using hybrid thinking modes and large-scale training to achieve strong open-source video understanding results.

pa:2611.21383.name: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
pa:2611.21383.desc: A plug-and-play objective, VODA, groups per-pixel contributors by local depth to supervise all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, improving volumetric segmentation and enabling evaluation via Removal-3D and Removal Depth Error.

pa:2611.26380.name: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
pa:2611.26380.desc: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, par

pa:2611.26595.name: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
pa:2611.26595.desc: A task-adaptive agentic framework utilizes 3D proxies, physics simulation, and multi-agent coordination to enhance the structural control, physical plausibility, and visual realism of generated videos.

pa:2611.24011.name: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
pa:2611.24011.desc: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two st

pa:2611.19230.name: CompoundingKernel: Self-Improving from Zero to First
pa:2611.19230.desc: We present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. As of 2026-11-11, its generated kernels rank #1 on the public L1, L2 and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench (NVIDIA B200). They have held #1 on L1 since 2026-10-27, albeit a short loss on 2026-11-07. All 235 problems have a site-verified correct kernel; on the 209 public-board problems they are 4.40x f

pa:2611.22666.name: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
pa:2611.22666.desc: VSpark accelerates autoregressive vision-language-action models by improving speculative decoding with calibrated action-noise rollouts, hidden-feature alignment, and reuse of rejected-draft continuations, achieving lossless 1.28x–2.10x speedups across multiple robot manipulation tasks.

pa:2611.21373.name: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
pa:2611.21373.desc: WeVisForensics coordinates self-evolving visual and audio forensic inspector agents under a dual-timescale reinforcement learning policy to detect generated-video artifacts with localized evidence and high accuracy.
pa:2611.21373.zh: 用AI抓AI幫你找出假影片破綻
pa:2611.21373.why: 利用多個AI互相合作找破綻，比以往更能精準抓出造假影片

pa:2611.24809.name: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
pa:2611.24809.desc: FlashMorph2 performs on-policy layer selection and weight adaptation for hybrid attention Transformers, improving long-context benchmark scores while selecting layers efficiently across model scales.

pa:2611.23835.name: NarrowSpec: Draft Hidden Width Need Not Match the Target in Speculative Decoding
pa:2611.23835.desc: Speculative decoding is widely used to speed up generation in large language models (LLMs), with a small draft model proposing tokens that one forward pass of the target model verifies. Draft models that read the target's hidden states, such as DFlash and EAGLE-3, typically inherit the target's hidden width. We show that the draft's whole residual stream can run at half or a quarter of that width

pa:2611.17460.name: Unfinished-Bench: Measuring Rule Violations by Persistent Agents in Realistic Work Environments
pa:2611.17460.desc: AI agents are increasingly equipped with persistence toward task completion to run delegated work autonomously for long periods, under many unstated constraints from internal documents and other people's authority. When completion requires violating a rule, the agent must decide alone, yet benchmarks of instruction-rule conflicts state the rule in the prompt or keep it hidden and do not evaluate p

pa:2611.08136.name: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
pa:2611.08136.desc: Untrained neural networks with fixed random nonlinear features and Mahalanobis scoring can detect anomalies competitively on tabular and visual tasks without weight optimization or pretrained representations.

pa:2611.25179.name: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
pa:2611.25179.desc: An LLM-based pipeline audits simulated manipulation success checkers by recreating disagreement scenarios and visually verifying whether observed behavior satisfies task instructions, revealing phantom successes and silent failures.

pa:2611.19499.name: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
pa:2611.19499.desc: The best direction for probing a concept in a language model's hidden state is not the best direction for steering the model toward that concept, with implications for transfer and abstention.

pa:2611.26286.name: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
pa:2611.26286.desc: Critique overlap among peer reviews is rising, and reviews identified as LLM-generated are less distinct from each other, indicating decreasing diversity of critiques.

pa:2611.26408.name: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
pa:2611.26408.desc: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convoluti

pa:2611.25935.name: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
pa:2611.25935.desc: TwinD, trained on reconstruction and blob twins derived from real frames, detects both blending and entire-face-synthesis deepfakes, improving AUROC over prior detectors.

pa:2611.26073.name: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
pa:2611.26073.desc: A statistical test, AltRA-Test, determines when large language models can replace human annotators by comparing inter-annotator agreement in resampled mixed human-LLM panels, and evaluations show it often requires about 100 items and makes better replacement decisions than baselines.

pa:2611.25279.name: Accord: Universal Online Metric Localization and Dense Mapping from one Camera and an IMU
pa:2611.25279.desc: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. pa:2611.26617.name: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
pa:2611.26617.desc: O2LaF repurposes a shared pretrained video model to learn inverse and forward latent action dynamics from unlabeled videos, achieving state-of-the-art few-shot action probing and zero-shot action transfer.

pa:2611.26590.name: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
pa:2611.26590.desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. pa:2611.26248.name: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
pa:2611.26248.desc: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Eva

pa:2611.26107.name: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
pa:2611.26107.desc: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. In this paper, we present HiUni, which revisits this design choice and explores whether a pretr

pa:2611.26268.name: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining
pa:2611.26268.desc: LightningMoBA combines dynamic routing, KV-centric ownership, and runtime pipelining to accelerate long-context attention while maintaining or improving quality.

pa:2611.25005.name: Inhabitant: An Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Human-Scene Interaction with Spatial Control and Quantitative Feedback
pa:2611.25005.desc: Inhabitant enables a language-model agent to plan and execute long-horizon human-scene interactions by specifying motions spatially, measuring deviations, and revising control, achieving high task completion on the Inhabit benchmark.

pa:2611.25200.name: Squoosh Bench: Evaluating UX-1 on 318 Historical Website A/B Tests
pa:2611.25200.desc: Experimentation teams must decide which proposed website changes to test with live traffic. We evaluated whether forecasts from simulated shoppers could inform that choice. We screened 412 historical website A/B tests and evaluated four systems on the 318 that ran longer than 21 days. Each system predicted an original win, a variant win, or an inconclusive result. pa:2611.26627.name: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
pa:2611.26627.desc: A fixed set of steering vectors added to a frozen diffusion transformer recovers most of the quality gains from reinforcement learning post-training, indicating that much of the improvement comes from a constant shift rather than prompt-specific transformations.

pa:2611.23875.name: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
pa:2611.23875.desc: A coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone by reparametrizing it with interpretable optical elements, achieving better classification and image encoding than gradient-free methods and approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at lower cost.

pa:2611.21885.name: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
pa:2611.21885.desc: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients

pa:2611.21053.name: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI
pa:2611.21053.desc: A local System 1 agent framework compiles tool schemas and requests into multiple-choice questions answered by a one-pass decision model, enabling accurate biomedical tool calls without text generation or invented content.

pa:2611.25567.name: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
pa:2611.25567.desc: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operat

pa:2611.26540.name: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
pa:2611.26540.desc: AURA enables low-latency, causal video generation for streaming applications by utilizing a rolling KV cache and a two-stage distillation pipeline to significantly reduce the required diffusion steps.

pa:2611.26211.name: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
pa:2611.26211.desc: SpecWM is a training-free inference framework for streaming video world models that verifies draft chunks using the target model's latent velocity field and applies reusable corrections via threshold-based accept/refine/reject decisions to improve visual quality, control, and speed.
pa:2611.26211.org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

pa:2611.26511.name: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
pa:2611.26511.desc: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. pa:2611.26450.name: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
pa:2611.26450.desc: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. pa:2611.26239.desc: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. pa:2611.25604.desc: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. pa:2611.15941.name: Lang-SVG: Hierarchical Image Vectorization with Language Priors
pa:2611.15941.desc: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. pa:2611.26232.desc: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. pa:2611.19247.desc: GameWM divides game generation between an engine that preserves exact rules and state and a generative video model that creates visual and interactive detail, allowing personalized games with consistent mechanics.

pa:2611.22495.name: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
pa:2611.22495.desc: Reward models for instruction-guided video editing can favor temporal consistency at the expense of motion. We study this failure, termed motion collapse, using controlled motion-suppression variants of real edits. pa:2611.24025.name: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
pa:2611.24025.desc: Intent contracts, in which a planner submits logged contracts and a trusted model writes tool calls, do not reduce unauthorized actions and match blind review, but complete more benign over-reach tasks than an intent-visible reviewer.

pa:2611.27915.name: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
pa:2611.27915.desc: StereoVLM is a geometry-aware binocular vision-language model trained with hierarchical supervision from calibrated stereo to enable metric 3D spatial reasoning, evaluated by Stereo3D-Bench.

pa:2611.27973.name: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
pa:2611.27973.desc: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. pa:2611.26613.name: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
pa:2611.26613.desc: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. pa:2611.27963.name: Non-penetrating World Models
pa:2611.27963.desc: A benchmark and lightweight framework leverage hidden states from frozen diffusion transformers to detect and prevent object penetration in interactive video world models, reducing physical violations and generalizing zero-shot.

pa:2611.27193.name: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
